intervals.label: installation and commissioning at SNOLAB
intervals.note: Move to SNOLAB in 2012 (Fermilab news). The dissertation expected data taking 'near the end of 2012'; the CosPA 2013 abstract says the chamber 'began operating in summer 2013', and the first PICO-60 run dates from June 2013.
intervals.quote: Work began at Fermilab in 2005, and, after extensive testing, the detector was moved to SNOLAB in 2012.

intervals.label: run 1 (CF3I)
intervals.quote: We report results from the first run of PICO-60, with a dark matter exposure of 3415 kg-days taken at SNOLAB between June 2013 and May 2014.

name: PICO-60
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

COUPP-60 and PICO-60 are one detector: Fermilab news (2017) says 'The PICO-60 detector was originally called COUPP-60'. The Atlas therefore keeps one experiment record (A4: one canonical entity per real thing) with COUPP-60 as an alias and the Fermilab commissioning as its first interval.
Several PICO-60 analyses beyond the three limit papers exist (photon-mediated interactions, inelastic dark matter, fermionic absorption); they are recorded as result records.

summary.plain: PICO-60 was the largest dark-matter bubble chamber of its day, built at Fermilab as COUPP-60 and run at SNOLAB from 2013 to 2017, first with CF3I and then with C3F8. Its results gave the strongest limits then on dark matter that couples to the spin of the proton.
summary.technical: Superheated bubble chamber (nominal size '60') in a synthetic fused-silica jar with water buffer, stereo cameras and piezoelectric sensors, in a water tank in the SNOLAB Ladder Labs. Run 1 CF3I (36.8 kg, 3415 kg-days, 92.8 analysed live days; June 2013-May 2014); run 2 C3F8 (52 kg; 1167 kg-days at 3.3 keV, then 1404 kg-days at 2.45 keV, thresholds as low as 1.2 keV). SD WIMP-proton limit 2.5e-41 cm^2 at 25 GeV (final exposure). Decommissioned after summer 2017; its water tank now houses PICO-40L.
